review_candidates.description: If you’re interested in this role, please apply in English and include an English version of your Resume/CV. The Role Joining Moderna means advancing mRNA science to transform medicine. Work with exceptional global teams on a broad pipeline and build a career that makes a real difference for patients. Moderna is strengthening its international business services hub in Warsaw, supporting our growing global operations. We welcome professionals ready to help advance our mission and shape the future of mRNA medicines. Based in Warsaw as an individual contributor, you will lead worldwide Clinical Trial Application (CTA) operations outside the United States, excluding US Investigational New Drug (IND) submissions. You will provide operational and regulatory support across global programs, connecting cross-functional teams, contract research organizations (CROs), and Health Authority submission activities while ensuring compliance with country-specific CTA requirements. Your remit will also include Development Safety Update Report (DSUR) submission oversight and supporting the creation of Development Medicinal Products in the xEVMPD system. Here’s What You’ll Do Lead end-to-end global CTA operations outside the US, coordinating cross-functional activities and submission tracking across regions. Bring together operational planning, regulatory requirements, and execution to support timely, compliant submissions to Health Authorities. Partner with Global Regulatory Leads (GRLs) to ensure program strategies are aligned across regions and reflected in CTA submission plans, timelines, and operational priorities. Oversee and coordinate CROs to support timely CTA delivery, aligning submission activities and deliverables with program needs and maintaining clear visibility of progress across global regions. Oversee the preparation, review, and execution of CTA submission packages, managing associated timelines and operational plans. Coordinate cross-functional inputs and delivery to Health Authorities, ensuring packages meet country-specific CTA requirements. Manage regulatory databases and sponsor-side administration within CTIS, IRAS, and Veeva RIM, ensuring accurate tracking, effective submission management, and complete regulatory records throughout CTA execution. Oversee regulatory query management, coordinating cross-functional and CRO contributions to Health Authority responses and driving timely resolution while maintaining alignment with the relevant program strategy. Maintain high-quality regulatory documentation and dossier management practices, supporting compliance, record completeness, and audit readiness across global CTA activities. Support the cross-functional team with DSUR submission oversight, coordinating relevant operational inputs and monitoring submission progress to support timely delivery. Support the creation of Development Medicinal Products in the xEVMPD system, working with cross-functional colleagues to ensure the associated regulatory information is accurately captured. The key Moderna Mindsets you’ll need to succeed in the role: "We act with dynamic range, driving strategy and execution at the same time at every step.” You will connect program-level regulatory strategy with detailed operational execution, moving between global stakeholder coordination, CRO oversight, submission planning, and regulatory query resolution. Success means maintaining a clear view of program objectives while ensuring the accuracy and completeness of each submission and regulatory record. “We digitize everywhere possible using the power of code to maximize our impact on patients.” You will apply a digital mindset to regulatory systems, information quality, and submission management. This includes exploring opportunities to work with generative AI tools to support regulatory information retrieval, document workflows, and operational tracking, with appropriate human review, confidentiality safeguards, and attention to applicable regulatory requirements. Here’s What You’ll Need (Basic Qualifications) At least bachelor’s degree in life science or related discipline 5+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical industry. 4+ years of experience in Regulatory CTA Experience in the preparation/submission of regulatory documentation to support clinical trials applications/amendments in the European Union Good understanding of the Regulation (EU) 536/2014 and Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) (Amendment) Regulations 2025 Proven ability to work within multi-functional teams, building strong and productive relationships across an organization. A desire to be part of a high-growth, transformational company that is Bold, Relentless, Curious, and Collaborative Proficiency in English (verbal and/or written) required due to global collaboration needs Our Working Model As we build our company, we have always believed an in-person culture is critical to our success. Moderna champions the significant benefits of in-office collaboration by embracing a 70/30 work model. This 70% in-office structure helps to foster a culture rich in innovation, teamwork, and direct mentorship. Join us in shaping a world where every interaction is an opportunity to learn, contribute, and make a meaningful impact. Moderna is a smoke-free, alcohol-free, and drug-free work environment. Pay & Benefits At Moderna, we believe that when you feel your best, you can do your best work. That’s why our benefits and well-being resources are designed to support you—at work, at home, and everywhere in between. We are seeking a hands-on Human Resources Manager to support our growing federal contracting workforce. Our work depends on strong, compliant teams and effective support for employees working across contracts, locations, and states. We value practical problem-solving, close partnership with our clients, and HR practices that help employees and the organization succeed. This role combines strategic planning with direct, hands-on responsibility for employee relations, compliance, benefits, onboarding, and workforce support. You will partner with executive leadership, operations, Growth, Talent Acquisition, and proposal teams to support organizational expansion and contract requirements. A central focus is Service Contract Act (SCA) compliance. The successful candidate will advise on wage determinations, health and welfare benefits, fringe requirements, labor category mapping, workforce planning, and contract transitions. The position supports a nationwide, geographically dispersed workforce and requires travel throughout the United States of approximately 15%. The annual compensation range is $100,000–$145,000. Offers are based on factors including location, skills, experience, training, certifications, and organizational needs. Qualifications A bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field is required, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Candidates must have at least five years of HR experience as an overhead, non-billable employee within a small or mid-sized federal government contractor, at least three years administering SCA contracts, and at least five years managing an HR team of two or more employees. Applicants should bring broad experience in employee relations, benefits administration, performance management, regulatory compliance, and employee lifecycle management. Strong knowledge of federal and state employment laws, experience supporting employees across multiple states in a virtual environment, and the ability to travel nationally are required. U.S. citizenship is required. Selected applicants will undergo a government security investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information and obtain a government-granted security clearance. Background checks may include criminal history, employment and education verification, drug testing, and creditworthiness. Preferred qualifications include SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP, PHR, or SPHR certification; residence within a two-hour commute of Northern Virginia; experience with Rippling or a comparable HRIS; and experience supporting rapid growth, contract transitions, and Business Development, Capture, or Proposal teams. Knowledge of government contracting regulations and workforce compliance is also preferred. Responsibilities Lead, coach, and develop HR staff; establish policies and practices aligned with business needs; and advise leaders on employee relations and organizational effectiveness. Manage investigations, performance concerns, corrective actions, conflict resolution, and manager coaching. Oversee onboarding, promotions, transfers, separations, employee records, orientation, benefits enrollment, and compliance training. Administer SCA wage determinations and health and welfare requirements, map labor categories to the SCA Directory of Occupations, and provide compliance and pricing guidance during proposal development. Support workforce planning, contract mobilizations, transitions, and onboarding. Oversee benefits, leave administration, audits, reporting, and risk management. Monitor legislative changes and ensure compliance with wage and hour rules, FMLA, ADA, and other applicable requirements. Support OSHA programs, including safety training, incident reporting, recordkeeping, and coordination with regulatory stakeholders. Deliver consistent HR guidance and engagement support across states and contract locations. Benefits This role offers the opportunity to shape HR practices in a growing federal contracting organization, lead a dedicated HR team, and work closely with executive and operational leaders. Compensation is competitive and determined according to relevant qualifications and business considerations. Specific benefits details are available during the hiring process. Equal Opportunity BDR Solutions, LLC is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome protected veterans, individuals with disabilities, and all applicants protected by applicable law, ordinance, or regulation. Applicants who need an accommodation may contact TalentAcquisition@bdrsolutionsllc.com.

review_candidates.title: Global Head of People & Talent
review_candidates.description: Global Head of People and Talent Location: San Ramon, CA (Hybrid; 3 days per week in office) Compensation: $150,000 – $200,000 + up to 20% bonus About ARIVE And The Role ARIVE is a privately held, founder-led fintech transforming digital mortgage originations with the industry's first Wholesale Originations Marketplace. We empower local loan originators to deliver best-fit, personalized mortgages from a vast network of lenders. Our feature-rich loan origination platform is mission-critical for the tens of thousands of originators who rely on it every day. We are profitable and growing rapidly - currently ~45 employees in the US and 130+ engineers at our India subsidiary - and building the leadership team and organizational design that will carry ARIVE through its next phase of growth and scale. We are looking for a Global Head of People and Talent - a strategic, hands-on leader and trusted advisor to the CEO who will own ARIVE's people function end-to-end, including organizational design, talent acquisition, employee development, performance, and culture. You will partner closely with functional heads to build a high-performance organization, collaborate openly with employees across every level and geography, and embody the ARIVE core values and culture in everything you do - leading the people function to ensure ARIVE remains agile and nimble, aligns employee expectations, and strengthens engagement through rapid growth. Core Responsibilities Serve as a trusted advisor to the CEO on organizational design, key hiring decisions, talent management and people-related matters that shape the company; bring market intelligence, peer benchmarks, and best-practice recommendations that inform decisions and translate strategy into a multi-year workforce plan across the US and India. Implement organizational design across functions in close partnership with each functional leader - team structures, leveling, people development, and succession planning - and own the operating rhythm for planning, performance, and talent review cycles. Design and run performance management, calibration, and feedback cycles that raise the bar and help every employee do their best work. Operationalize ARIVE's compensation framework - base, bonus, and benefits - tied directly to performance reviews and measurable business and individual outcomes, with regular market research and benchmarking against SaaS peers and comparable companies to inform leadership decisions. Manage health, retirement, PTO, and employee wellness programs with the same rigor applied to every other investment. Build and maintain HR policies, employee handbooks, job titles and descriptions, mandatory state trainings (anti-harassment, workplace safety, and other state-required programs), and compliance controls across multi-state US operations and intercompany coordination with our India subsidiary. Oversee employee records, contracts, and the full employee lifecycle with discretion and sound judgment on sensitive matters - investigations, performance exits, and leadership changes. Elevate ARIVE's employer brand across the tech ecosystem and our key talent markets; lead the US recruiting team on new hires and provide oversight and alignment for India hiring with India HR leadership. Design new-hire onboarding and employee development programs that accelerate time-to-impact and growth, and anchor every joiner in ARIVE's mission, values, and ways of working; create career pathing, internal mobility, and development frameworks - including manager and leadership capability building - that help employees grow with the company. Champion recognition, celebration, and internal communication programs that reinforce ARIVE's values through direct engagement with employees at every level and geography; own engagement measurement and listening programs (pulse, engagement, exit) and the response programs that follow. Partner with the CEO and functional leaders to bring AI-forward thinking to workforce strategy - assess how AI is reshaping roles, identify reskilling and upskilling needs, and embed AI tools and practices into how the people function itself operates (recruiting, onboarding, performance, HR ops). What We're Looking For 15+ years experience in Human Resources. 5+ years in senior people leadership roles, with meaningful time in high-growth technology companies. Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree or SHRM/HRCI certification a plus. Experience scaling people functions across distributed teams and multiple locations or time zones as the senior-most leader or a strong second-in-command ready to step into the top role. Proven ability to design high-performance organizations in partnership with strong functional leaders. Strong command of compensation strategy in technology companies. Ability to operate as both a trusted advisor to a founder-CEO and a hands-on builder who will write the people operations handbook, run calibrations, and stay close to the day-to-day people decisions across the company. Exceptional judgment and discretion with sensitive people data and related matters. Data-driven decision-making — reaches for the numbers before the narrative, balanced with empathy and sound instinct. AI-forward perspective on how technology is reshaping work, roles, and the people function itself - with practical experience deploying AI tools and frameworks within an HR organization. What We Offer Compensation: The US base salary range for this full-time position is $150,000 – $200,000 + up to 20% performance-based bonus. The position is eligible for performance-based equity compensation. Our salary ranges are determined by location, level, and role; individual compensation will be determined by experience, skills, and job-related knowledge. Location: San Francisco Bay Area, CA (Hybrid): 2-3 days per week in office, with remote flexibility on other days. Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance. 401(k) plan with employer match. Generous PTO policy. Logistics Must be based in the San Francisco Bay Area and able to work from ARIVE's San Ramon HQ 3 days per week. Relocation assistance available for eligible candidates. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position. Note: ARIVE is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by local, state, or federal laws, rules, or regulations.

review_candidates.title: Fresh Graduate Electrical Engineer
review_candidates.description: Company Description EnergyX Egypt, founded in 2018 and based in Giza, specializes in reliable energy infrastructure for industrial and commercial applications. The company delivers DC power systems, advanced battery solutions, and high-performance charging technologies that support critical operations. EnergyX also provides on-grid and off-grid solar design and installation services, enabling clients to adopt sustainable energy solutions. Working at EnergyX offers exposure to modern power systems and renewable energy projects in a growing, innovation-driven environment. Role Description This is a full-time remote role for a Fresh Graduate Electrical Engineer. The role involves assisting in the design and analysis of DC power systems, battery configurations, and solar power solutions under the guidance of senior engineers. Typical tasks include preparing technical drawings and documentation, performing basic calculations for power distribution and load flow, and supporting system testing and validation. The engineer will collaborate with cross-functional teams to review specifications, follow industry standards, and contribute to project implementation and performance monitoring. The position provides learning opportunities through involvement in real projects, participation in technical meetings, and continuous skill development in modern electrical and renewable energy systems. Qualifications Strong foundational knowledge in Electrical Engineering and Electricity concepts, with the ability to apply theory to practical industrial and commercial applications. Ability to assist with Electrical Design tasks, including basic schematics, layouts, and component selection for power-related projects. Understanding of Power Systems, including generation, transmission, and distribution principles, and their application in DC and solar systems. Basic knowledge of Power Distribution practices, safety standards, and relevant codes used in industrial and commercial environments. Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a closely related field, preferably recently graduated. Proficiency with engineering tools and software (e.g., AutoCAD or similar CAD tools; familiarity with power system analysis software is a plus). Good analytical and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail and the ability to learn quickly in a remote work setting. Effective written and verbal communication skills in English; ability to collaborate with diverse teams and follow technical instructions. Interest in renewable energy, solar systems, and sustainable power solutions; any internship or academic project in these areas is an advantage.

review_candidates.title: Founding Forward Deployed Engineer
review_candidates.description: Why we’re opening this position Claims handling has been the biggest pain point in insurance for decades. For insurers, the direct and indirect cost runs to 800B every year. For customers, it's the #1 driver of dissatisfaction. Insurers and brokers alike all agree AI will solve this, but they can't scale it. Nor are the generic AI workflow vendors any match for the messy reality of claims handling. As Warren Buffett put it himself: "insurance always looks easier than it is". Ellis was founded by insurtech veterans who have built and scaled fully automated AI claims handling. We're now building the leading vertical AI solution for it - designed from the ground up to integrate with systems no API can touch, and to reach human-grade accuracy in weeks instead of years . Doing this requires building one of the most sophisticated back-office automation products anywhere, where AI autonomy meets the complex reality of insurance claims. It requires redefining what AI engineering can actually do. Ellis is supported by top tier investors and successful business angels such as the founders of french unicorn Qonto and belgian unicorn Aikido. The position itself As a Founding Forward Deployed Engineer, you own the activity everything else depends on: delivery. And it's one of the hardest challenges in our space. How do we compress implementation cycles and ship a product that hits human-grade accuracy and reliability in weeks - when everyone else who has ever tried needed quarters, or years? On the one hand, this means actually getting deals live: During the selling phase, you work with the revenue team to scope the product offer. Once the deal is signed, you take ove r and: Build a deep understanding of your client's process Design the target solution Design the roll-out process Integrate with our client's systems of record Once you're running in production, you drive the hypercare phase. Every step of the way, you're: Working closely with the engineering team to help them build the features you need. In the trenches, working side by side with the founders. Using AI to speed up the process - from process mining to automatically detecting the root causes of AI errors. But on the other hand - and more importantly - it means you're building the foundations of Ellis' business: Building our core product , turning your learnings into features and the solutions you've delivered into repeatable offerings: your custom build for today's client should be tomorrow's off-the-shelf product. Building a system to accelerate deal delivery by 10x , so Ellis can unlock the next stage of its growth. To get deals live in weeks, you'll work out how we automate large chunks of the process, and create AI agents built to do the heavy lifting. This is arguably even more important than the AI agents that automate claims themselves. Shaping the company vision : to your left and to your right, engineering and revenue will rely on your opinion to set their roadmaps. Who we’re looking for If you’re excited by now, it's already a good sign. When it comes to your competencies: A technical appetite, whether from your studies or your work experience. You'll be shipping production config code (Python and YAML) - and even if you're using AI to do it, we need you to deeply understand what you're building.  Exposure to one of the two sides of our business: Complex enterprise transformations Fast-paced startups Bonus points if you've had exposure to the financial services industry, or if you've founded your own business before. When it comes to your approach to the job: A strong sense of ownership , work ethic, and a low-ego mindset: at Ellis, the best idea always wins, not the loudest voice. Excitement for open-ended problems without predetermined solutions. You've got all the support you need, but you're the one who makes the magic happen. You take your job seriously but not yourself - what's the point of all this if we're not having fun? What we offer in exchange Beyond working on one of the most interesting problems in AI automation, alongside an ambitious founding team, we also offer: A competitive salary and benefits package. Support for your growth - we pay for training, events, etc. A flexible remote work policy. How to apply: Send your resume at talent@ellisclaims.ai
